_comment: How the ground gives way, and in what shapes (design 5.3).
`reach` is a RADIUS in blocks, not an area, so doubling it is four times the ground. Each shape spends
it as its own shape wants -- a fissure's length, a bowl's radii, a bolt's whole span, a shaft's depth --
and draws its other dimensions from it, so this is the one number that says how big.
`pace` is how long the falling takes against the walked one: under one is quicker, over one is slower.
It moves the stagger between neighbouring blocks, the length of a crumbling stage and how often the
swathe is rescanned, all together, because moving any one of them alone is visible as the wrong thing.
The three-second warning is on neither dial and is not meant to be.
`shapes` weights the seven against each other; a shape left out never happens. The fissure is the
commonest because it reads best on the most ground. The square is one in a hundred because a thing that
unnatural stops being unnatural if it is common -- it is meant to be the one you tell somebody about.
`fury` is what the top of `tectonics` in the price list makes of the two dials. Unwalked, like the top
of every other inflicted register: nothing sees it without a badly broken Age.
